one_liner: Header-only C++17 SSE/AVX2 MT19937, Xoroshiro128+ and MSWS; AVX2 MT19937 matches std::mt19937 output and generates it about 8x faster.
what_it_does: A header-only C++17 library (include pxart/pxart.hpp) with scalar, SSE (simd128) and AVX2 (simd256) versions of MT19937, Xoroshiro128+ and Middle Square Weyl Sequence (MSWS), plus fast uniform-float and bounded-integer conversions. The SIMD engines return a whole __m128i/__m256i per call, and pxart::simd256::uniform<float>(rng) turns that into 8 floats, so callers either write intrinsics code or drain the vector through a small buffer. Default-constructed or default_seeder{seed}-seeded MT19937 engines produce exactly the std::mt19937 sequence; the repo's tests check 10 million outputs of the AVX2 engine against std::mt19937.
how_it_is_fast: For MT19937 it vectorizes the state twist of a single generator (Agner Fog's technique): 8 consecutive state words are updated per AVX2 instruction, and a copy of the first new block stored past the end of the state array handles the wrap-around, so output order is unchanged. Xoroshiro128+ and MSWS instead run several independent instances side by side in the vector lanes (multi-stream), so their SIMD output differs from the scalar sequence. Uniform floats are made by OR-ing the top 23 (float) or 52 (double) random bits into the exponent of 1.0 and subtracting 1, and bounded integers use a multiply-shift instead of a division.
when_to_use: Code bound to the std::mt19937 sequence (reproducible simulations, saved seeds) that needs much higher throughput on x86 with AVX2 or SSE2
Bulk fills of 32-bit randoms or floats, e.g. Monte Carlo inner loops where you can consume 8 values per call or buffer them
SIMD kernels already written with AVX2 intrinsics that want random vectors directly in registers
Projects that want a tiny MIT header-only dependency, usable via build2, CMake or by copying the pxart/ folder
when_not_to_use: Non-x86 targets: SIMD paths are SSE/AVX2 intrinsics only; ARM or other platforms fall back to the scalar engines
When you need std <random> distributions on the vector engines: there are no normal, exponential or other non-uniform distributions

When you are free to change the generator and want maximum speed: pXart's own AVX2 Xoroshiro128+ beats its AVX2 MT19937 (0.74 s vs 1.15 s for 16 GiB in the thesis), and other siblings are faster still
Production code that needs maintenance or support: 3 stars, alpha build2 package, last commit January 2021
Exact unbiased bounded integers: the multiply-shift range reduction has a small bias the code itself calls an approximation

integration.dependencies: none (doctest for tests, perfevent for benchmarks)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17; README lists GCC, Clang, Intel, MinGW and MSVC as tested; SIMD headers compile only when __AVX2__ / __SSE2__ are defined (e.g. -march=native)
integration.platforms: any for scalar engines; x86-64 with SSE2 (simd128 MT19937) or AVX2 (simd256) for the vectorized engines
integration.thread_safety: not documented; engines are plain value types with no shared state, so use one instance per thread
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — scalar pxart::mt19937 and the SIMD versions reproduce the std::mt19937 sequence, but the SIMD engines return vectors, min()/max() are non-static, and the API (pxart::uniform, default_seeder) differs from std::mt19937 plus distributions

gotchas: pxart::simd256::xoroshiro128plus's default constructor leaves its state uninitialized, and its seeding constructor calls rng() eight times inside one _mm256_set_epi32 argument list, whose evaluation order is unspecified, so seeded streams can differ between compilers
The templated RNG&& seeding constructor of pxart::mt19937 is a better match than the copy constructor for a non-const lvalue, so 'pxart::mt19937 b{a};' seeds b from a's outputs instead of copying a
uniform<double> from a 32-bit engine only has 32 random bits (low mantissa bits are zero); uniform<float> uses 23 bits and returns [0,1)
The SIMD headers silently define nothing if compiled without AVX2/SSE2 flags; check the PXART_SUPPORT_SIMD256_* macros
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick pXart when you must keep the exact 32-bit std::mt19937 sequence and want a small C++17 header with AVX2/SSE paths; VMT19937 also covers mt19937_64 and AVX-512, and if the generator can change, SIMD xoshiro siblings (simdrng, Xoroshiro-style engines) or SHISHUA are faster.
verified_claims_summary: In the author's 2019 master's thesis (Jena), GCC 9.2.0 -O3 -march=native on a Core i7-7700K at 4.51 GHz, generating 16 GiB through a 16 KiB buffer took 9.29 s with libstdc++ std::mt19937, 5.79 s with Boost mt19937 and 1.15 s with pXart's AVX2 MT19937 (about 8.1x and 5.0x, derived from page data); scalar pXart MT19937 (7.61 s) beat STL but not Boost. In a 10^8-sample Monte Carlo pi run, using the AVX2 MT19937 through a buffer in scalar code took 0.15 s vs 0.53 s for STL with pXart's uniform conversion (about 3.5x, derived from page data).
status_note: Abandoned since January 2021 (3 stars, alpha cppget.org package), but MIT-licensed, header-only and small enough to vendor; the AVX2 MT19937 is tested bit-for-bit against std::mt19937.
